category: Founder thought leadership & B2B referral pipeline (design/marketing agency)
title: A Pune B2B design agency made founder LinkedIn its #2 pipeline source — and de-risked lumpy referrals
content: SITUATION: A 14-person Pune B2B marketing-and-design agency billed ₹1.1cr/year, with ~80% of leads from referrals and the founder's word-of-mouth. Referrals were dangerously lumpy: Q2 brought 11 qualified leads, Q3 just 4 — a 64% drop with no marketing lever to pull. The founder posted on LinkedIn on mood, 2-3 times a month to 400 followers, so nothing compounded and a slow quarter meant an empty pipeline. ACTION: We turned thought leadership into a system, not a mood. He shipped 4 posts/week, each a teardown of one real (anonymised) SaaS landing page or rebrand, closing with a single specific takeaway and zero pitch. Every teardown was repurposed into a 90-second YouTube Short and a WhatsApp + email broadcast to ~60 past clients and warm intros. Cost: ₹1.2L/month — a part-time editor (₹35K) plus the founder's 5 hours/week. OUTCOME: Over 5 months, followers grew 400 to 5,800, the average teardown hit ~9,000 impressions, and inbound DMs converted into 7 retainers worth ₹38L in annual contract value (~₹5.4L each). Referral dependence fell from 80% to 58% of pipeline, with thought leadership now the #2 source at ~30% — the lumpiness was finally hedged.
lesson: Founder thought leadership only compounds as a fixed cadence in one repeatable format — inspiration-driven posting never accrues. The leverage is repurposing: one teardown becomes a LinkedIn post, a YouTube Short and a WhatsApp/email broadcast, so 5 founder-hours buys a week of multi-channel reach. And the pipeline isn't the impressions — it's the inbound DMs you personally reply to. For a referral-dependent agency, this is insurance: a system you can dial up in a slow quarter, not a mood you wait on.
